name: agent-bridge-concurrent-relay
description: Tier-P F1 relay-resilience scenario: install + provision agent-bridge on a fresh box, then drive the REAL credential-relay server through port CONTENTION and assert the binding guarantee behind the duplicate-daemon relay bug -- when a second party contends for the relay's port (the classic case is a racing daemon spawned by a concurrent sessionStart-hook reinstall), the relay must still come up (reclaim the port, or fall back to an OS-assigned ephemeral one) and publish the port it actually bound; a relay left silently unbound breaks all credential forwarding over the SSH tunnel. Checks: (dynamic-default-bind) port 0 -> OS-assigned ephemeral, running, publishes the real port; (live-occupant-ephemeral-fallback) a live, unevictable occupant holds a pinned port -> the relay falls back to an ephemeral port, comes up, and publishes a DIFFERENT real port, never left silently unbound. FIDELITY: a fully live 'two real daemons race the installer and CodeSpace auth keeps working end-to-end' assertion needs two installed daemons + an SSH -R relay + a remote git op (a Tier-E, box-in-the-loop concern for the wider chaos rig); this Tier-P probe proves the relay-bind RESILIENCE the auth-survives guarantee is built on. The probe is portable stdlib-only (drives the real credential_relay server), so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Name-free / public.
